{{short description|Mexican physicist}}
'''Rosa Luz Alegría Escamilla''' (born 1949) is a Mexican [[physicist]] who was the first woman to serve in the [[Mexican Executive Cabinet]].

Alegría studied [[physics]] in the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM).  During her time at the university she got involved with UNAM's ''Consejo General de Huelga'' ("General Strike Council", CGH).

During [[Luis Echeverría]]'s presidency she started to work in the public service. [[President of Mexico|President]] [[José López Portillo]] appointed her [[under-secretary]] of planning and budget (''Subsecretaria de Programación y Presupuesto''), and later, on August 13, 1980, she was appointed [[Secretary of Tourism (Mexico)|Secretary of Tourism]], becoming the first female [[Secretary of State]] in Mexico.

Alegria's appointment as Secretary of State occurred in an administration famous for [[nepotism]].<ref>Riding, Alan. ''Distant Neighbors: A Portrait of the Mexicans'', Vintage (reprinted 1989),  {{ISBN|0-679-72441-9}} - p.128</ref><ref>José López Portillo (obituary), ''The Economist'', March 4, 2004 accessed at [http://www.econ.umn.edu/~julian/teaching/econ4311_2005/lopez_portillo.pdf] March 27, 2007</ref>
